name: Market data

subjectOf.text: ICO funding collapsed as a share of blockchain startup fundraising, falling from 80% to around 35% by August 2018, recovering only marginally to 40% to 50% between September 2018 and February 2019, and dropping to 20% in March 2019.
subjectOf.abstract: The percentage of ICOs in relation to total fundraising of blockchain startups dropped from 80% to around 35% in August 2018 and only marginally recovered between September 2018 and February 2019 at around 40% to 50% before dropping to 20% in March 2019.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Financial Technology and Hedge Funds (2019). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3409548

subjectOf.text: ICO issuance exceeded venture capital financing of startups for the first time in the second quarter of 2017, with $210 million invested through ICOs against $180 million invested through traditional venture capital funds.
subjectOf.abstract: In the second quarter of 2017, ICO issuances exceeded venture capital financing of start-ups for the first time,56 with $210 million invested in ICOs versus $180 million invested into start-ups via traditional venture capital funds.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Digital Asset Market Evolution (2020). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3606663

subjectOf.text: The DeFi lending market is highly concentrated: MakerDAO alone accounts for almost ninety percent of the total USD value locked in DeFi projects.
subjectOf.abstract: MakerDAO accounts for almost ninety percent of total USD value locked in DeFi projects.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Digital Asset Market Evolution (2020). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3606663
